title: Words English borrowed from around the world
examples: Which English words come from Hindi?
Where does the word shampoo come from?

figure.name: x-sort
figure.question: Where did English borrow it from?

explain.say: When you wash your hair, you are speaking Hindi! Look at the board: sham, poo. Shampoo comes from the Hindi word chāmpo, which means to press, as in a head massage. English is full of words borrowed from other languages.

draw.text: Words English borrowed from around the world

explain.say: A borrowed word is called a loanword, though English never gives them back! Look at the first group on the board: shampoo, jungle, pyjamas, bungalow, all from Hindi and Urdu. Have you worn pyjamas today?

draw.name: x-sort
draw.question: Where did English borrow it from?

explain.say: Look at the second group, from Arabic: algebra, sofa, magazine and zero. Algebra comes from al-jabr, from a famous maths book written in Baghdad over 1,000 years ago. What do you sit on to watch TV?

draw.name: x-sort
draw.question: Where did English borrow it from?

explain.say: Now look at the Japanese group. Here is tsunami on the board: tsu, na, mi. Tsu means harbour, and nami means wave: a harbour wave. Emoji and karaoke came from Japanese too. Which one have you used today?

Brilliant! Last group: tomato, chocolate and avocado came from Nahuatl, the language of the Aztecs in Mexico. Wow: English has borrowed words from hundreds of languages. Challenge: find one word in your kitchen that English borrowed!

faq.a: A loanword is a word one language takes from another, like English shampoo from Hindi or tsunami from Japanese.

faq.q: Which English words come from Hindi?
faq.a: Shampoo, jungle, pyjamas, bungalow, thug, cot and loot all came into English from Hindi or Urdu.

faq.q: Where does the word shampoo come from?
faq.a: It comes from Hindi chāmpo, meaning to press or massage, from head massages offered in India and brought to Britain in the 1700s.

faq.q: Which English words come from Arabic?
faq.a: Algebra, algorithm, sofa, magazine, zero and coffee came from Arabic, often through other languages like Spanish, Italian or Turkish.

faq.q: Does English lend words to other languages too?
faq.a: Yes. Words like computer, football, weekend and OK are used in many languages around the world.

facts: Algebra comes from al-jabr in the title of a maths book by al-Khwarizmi, written in Baghdad in the 800s.
Tomato, chocolate and avocado come from the Nahuatl words tomatl, xocolatl and ahuacatl.
